title: 10 Chinese-Friendly Companies Hiring in the US (2026)
summary: TikTok, ByteDance, Google, Tencent and 6 more: where they hire in the US, how many postings ask for Mandarin, posted pay, and what the H-1B data says.
body_markdown:
[中文版 →](https://simplify.jobs/blog/chinese-friendly-companies-us-zh?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


I came to the US at 19 for college, and that was also my first time in the US. So my first trip abroad was also the first day of school. I'm the first person in my family to study abroad, which means every application I've ever sent, from college to a PhD to jobs, I figured out on my own. No agency, no consultant, just me and way too many browser tabs.


Now I work at a job search company, which is a little funny. I can finally see the stuff I used to guess at: who's actually hiring in the US, where, and which postings ask for Mandarin. I really want to share what I can see, and my boss is okay with it (yes, I asked first). So here's the list I wish someone had sent me back then.


## What "Chinese-friendly" means here


I'm not judging company culture. I can't measure that from a database, and anyone who says they can is selling something. Instead, every company on this list meets at least two of these checks:


1. It has a real US office that's hiring now. Not a China job listed in English. I only counted postings with a US location.
2. Some of its US postings ask for Mandarin or Chinese. "Mandarin preferred" is the most honest signal you'll get that speaking Chinese is a plus, not something to hide.
3. It's a Chinese company, or a US company with a public track record of sponsoring visas.


Where the numbers come from: Simplify finds and lists openings from company career sites. I counted the US postings we tracked from November 2025 to October 2026. Reposts and multi-city listings count separately, so read these as "postings," not "roles." The language field is parsed from the job description, and I spot-checked a sample by hand. When I give a pay range, it's the typical posted range: the median low end and median high end of the ranges each company listed.


One thing to say clearly: speaking Chinese is not the same as getting sponsored. A company being Chinese doesn't promise a visa. Ask about sponsorship before you spend three rounds interviewing.


## The list


### 1.[TikTok](https://simplify.jobs/c/TikTok?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has about 1,800 open US roles at TikTok.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/TikTok?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


The most US postings on this list: about 3,500 in the past year, 160 asking for Chinese, and 678 internships, mostly in San Jose, then Los Angeles, Seattle and New York. In October alone, about 5,400 Simplify users applied, and 43% of those who answered said they need sponsorship. TikTok had 412 new H-1B approvals in FY2025 ([NFAP analysis of USCIS data](https://nfap.com/studies/h-1b-petitions-and-denial-rates-in-fy-2025/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ). Since January 2026, its US data business has been a majority American-owned joint venture (ByteDance keeps 19.9%), so which team you join matters.


### 2.[ByteDance](https://simplify.jobs/c/ByteDance?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) (including the Seed team behind Seedance)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 571 open US roles at ByteDance.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/ByteDance?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


676 US postings in the past year, 31 asking for Chinese and 167 internships, mostly in San Jose and Seattle. A lot of the AI research hiring sits here, including the Seed team behind the Seedance video model. 46% of its Simplify applicants in October said they need sponsorship, the highest of the three big names here, and it had 449 new H-1B approvals in FY2025.


### 3.[Google](https://simplify.jobs/c/Google?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has about 1,700 open US roles at Google.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/Google?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


Google is here for sponsorship, not Mandarin: only 9 of about 18,000 US postings asked for it, but Google had more than 1,000 new H-1B approvals in FY2025, fourth among all employers (Amazon was first with about 4,600). If it feels like you meet a lot of Asian coworkers there, Google's[2024 Diversity Annual Report](https://belonging.google/diversity-annual-report/2024/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) backs that up: 45.7% of its US workforce and 51.4% of its US tech roles. It doesn't break out Chinese employees.


### 4.[Tencent](https://simplify.jobs/c/Tencent?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 62 open US roles at Tencent.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/Tencent?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


About one in six of its 320 US postings ask for Chinese, mostly in business development and sales. Palo Alto and Bellevue do AI research (Hunyuan, Tencent's AI model) and cloud. Los Angeles and Irvine are games, where the Lightspeed LA studio[cut about 80 roles in 2026](https://godisageek.com/2026/07/lightspeed-la-80-layoffs-last-sentinel/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) . Typical posted pay is $114,000 to $230,000 full-time and $27 to $52 an hour for interns. New H-1B approvals: 23 in FY2025, 13 in FY2026.


### 5.[JD.com](https://simplify.jobs/c/JINGDONG?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 56 open US roles at JD.com.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/JINGDONG?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


The highest Mandarin share on the list: 61 of 154 US postings, about 40%. But JD in the US is mostly logistics, with warehouses in Southern California, New Jersey and Georgia, plus a "JD Young" internship track where some titles literally say "(Mandarin Speaking)." Typical pay is $20 an hour for interns and $78,000 to $100,000 full-time. JD Logistics United States had 21 new H-1B approvals in FY2026, while JD's Silicon Valley tech entity has[mostly stopped sponsoring](https://www.ellis.com/visa-sponsors/jdcom-american-technologies-corporation?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


### 6.[SHEIN](https://simplify.jobs/c/SHEIN?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 16 open US roles at SHEIN.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/SHEIN?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


Founded in China, headquartered in Singapore, with its US business in Los Angeles: buyers, seller success, design, compliance and marketing, plus a data team in San Diego. 11 of 112 US postings ask for Chinese, typical full-time pay is $91,000 to $121,000, and it had only 6 new H-1B approvals in FY2026. Its US sales[dropped after the de minimis exemption ended](https://fashionunited.com/news/business/sheins-us-momentum-stalls-as-de-minimis-tariff-exemption-ends/2025101368667?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) in 2025.


### 7.[DiDi](https://simplify.jobs/c/DiDi-Global?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 11 open US roles at DiDi.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/DiDi-Global?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


None of its US postings ask for Chinese, but it has a real autonomous-driving team in San Jose,[there since 2017](https://techcrunch.com/2017/03/08/didi-us-research-lab/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) . It pays well ($141,000 to $282,000 full-time, $46 an hour for interns), but it's small and senior: the internship we saw was for PhD students. 3 new H-1B approvals in each of FY2025 and FY2026.


### 8.[XPENG](https://simplify.jobs/c/XPengMotors?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 13 open US roles at XPENG.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/XPengMotors?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


The best posted pay on the list: $179,000 to $304,000 full-time. Its Santa Clara team works on autonomous-driving models, AI infrastructure and robotics ([annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1810997/000119312526157849/d36361d20f.htm?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ), mostly in senior roles, with internships for master's and PhD students. 6 of 50 US postings ask for Chinese, and one program manager role[requires Mandarin](https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/xpengmotors/jobs/8675326002?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) . 8 new H-1B approvals in FY2026.


### 9.[Baidu USA](https://simplify.jobs/c/Baidu-USA?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 25 open US roles at Baidu USA.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/Baidu-USA?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


A small Mountain View office: AI chips and compilers on the engineering side, AI and ad sales on the business side. Typical full-time pay is $106,000 to $170,000, and one ads internship called Mandarin "a must." The catch: no new H-1B approvals in FY2025 and none listed for FY2026 ([USCIS](https://www.uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/h-1b-employer-data-hub?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ), and in June 2026 the Pentagon[added Baidu to its "Chinese military companies" list](https://fortune.com/2026/06/08/pentagon-accuses-alibaba-baidu-byd-china-military-companies/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) , which limits defense contracts, not employees.


### 10.[BYD](https://simplify.jobs/c/BYD?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


As of November 2026, Simplify has 20 open US roles at BYD.[See them and apply →](https://simplify.jobs/c/BYD?ref=blog.simplify.jobs)


BYD doesn't sell passenger cars in the US. Its US business is electric buses and trucks, energy storage and electronics, centered on the Lancaster bus factory (now the RIDE brand, with[more than 750 employees](https://theautowire.com/2026/09/26/byd-american-factory-lancaster-law-slotkin-xi-visit/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ) and a Pasadena office. 8 of 29 US postings ask for Chinese, mostly engineering, manufacturing and finance roles. 7 new H-1B approvals in FY2026, not counting its separate electronics company.


Also checked but not on the list:[HoYoverse](https://simplify.jobs/c/Ho-Yoverse?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) (25 US postings, 2 asking for Chinese) and Temu's parent[PDD](https://simplify.jobs/c/PDDN?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) (70 US postings, none asking for Chinese).


## The visa part, honestly


I'm not an immigration lawyer, and I'll stay in my lane here. Two things changed recently, and they're worth reading about from the source:


- The $100,000 H-1B fee: a September 2025 proclamation added it. According to USCIS guidance summarized by[NFAP](https://nfap.com/studies/h-1b-petitions-and-denial-rates-in-fy-2025/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) , it applies to new H-1B workers coming from outside the US. It doesn't apply to people who change status inside the US, like going from F-1 to H-1B. A newer fee rule was proposed in 2026 and isn't final, so check before you rely on this.
- The lottery is weighted by salary now. Starting with the FY2027 registration in March 2026, higher wage levels get more entries ([summary](https://www.hsfkramer.com/insights/2026-01/us-dhs-implements-weighted-selection-process-for-fy-2027-h-1b-cap-registrations?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ). For new grads, the offer amount now affects your odds, not only your luck.


For any company not covered above, you can look up its sponsorship history yourself in the[USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub](https://www.uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/h-1b-employer-data-hub?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) . It's free, and hardly anyone tells students about it. The new H-1B approval numbers for Tencent through BYD above come from there: "new employment" approvals, added up across each company's US entities, with data through September 30, 2026.


## How I'd use this list


At my last PM job, I had a lot of late-night meetings with our team in China, especially when we were working with the factory. Many of the people on the other end didn't speak English, so Mandarin wasn't a nice extra. It was how things moved forward. (My sleep schedule had other opinions.)


Treat Mandarin like any other skill. If a posting says "Mandarin preferred," put it near the top of your resume, not at the bottom next to "Microsoft Excel." Then apply to more places than feels comfortable. I applied everywhere myself with no help, and the hardest part wasn't any single application. It was doing it again and again without losing track. That part is what[Simplify Copilot](https://simplify.jobs/copilot?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) is for: it autofills applications and logs each one in your tracker, for free.


Good luck. 加油.


## Common questions


**Do Chinese companies in the US sponsor H-1B visas?** Some do, but the numbers vary a lot. In FY2026, JD Logistics United States had 21 new H-1B approvals, Tencent's US entities 13, XPENG 8, BYD 7 (not counting its electronics company), SHEIN 6 and DiDi 3, while Baidu USA had none listed. Ask about sponsorship before you start interviewing.


**Do I need to speak Mandarin to work at a Chinese company in the US?** Usually not. On Simplify, Mandarin shows up mostly in business development, sales, operations and logistics postings. About 40% of JD.com's US postings ask for it, and about one in six of Tencent's, but most engineering postings at these companies don't mention it, and none of DiDi's US postings did.


**Which of these companies pays the most?** By posted pay, XPENG: its full-time US postings typically listed about $179,000 to $304,000 a year. DiDi (about $141,000 to $282,000) and Tencent (about $114,000 to $230,000) come next.


**Does the $100,000 H-1B fee apply to F-1 students?** According to USCIS guidance summarized by NFAP, the fee applies to new H-1B workers coming from outside the US, not to people who change status inside the US, such as from F-1 to H-1B. A newer fee rule was proposed in 2026 and isn't final, so check the current rules first.


**Is TikTok still a Chinese company?** In January 2026, TikTok's US data business became a joint venture that's majority American-owned, and ByteDance keeps 19.9%. Which team you join can matter more than the logo.


**Where are most of these jobs?** Mostly in the Bay Area (San Jose, Palo Alto, Santa Clara, Mountain View), Los Angeles and Southern California, and Seattle and Bellevue. JD.com's logistics jobs are also in New Jersey and Georgia.
